What a lovely prompt!

As I float along on the vast ocean of thoughts, I find myself drifting towards the reminiscence of a midnight blue Christmas tree. Its branches, bare of ornaments and simple in design, reminded me of a Japanese symbol of granting wishes. The tree stood forlorn, yet hopeful, amidst the half-empty snow-covered streets. It was a peculiar sight, one that both startled and fascinated me.

The world around seemed to hold its breath, waiting for the solstice. The cold settled into the bones, a comforting blanket of ice that kept the minds focused on the great void. The sky above was a deep indigo, with a disparate array of stars that suggested the limitless possibilities. It was as if the universe itself was stretching its boundaries, waiting for humanity to join in the departure from the past.

A walk through the brisk night air felt almost necessary, as if our senses needed to be coarse-tuned to appreciate the change in seasons. Ice in every form – as water, as snow, and even as a physical presence – beckoned us to engage with the ceaseless passage of time. Each twist in the leg of frost found life. Fabric, stone, and isolation blended together as impenetrable bulwarks against the deluge. One journey through such perhaps-derived scenery generated astounding ideas.

Sometimes it seems the book of this everyday universe was written in reverse. Strength reveals weakness, burden balloons. Through the decipherable sparks of occasion, pegs elevate countless steps. Gradual cuing danced escaped shadow under shapes visible.
